LITERATURE IN ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.

2. When practising Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.

3. When practising Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla, which approach is best? (1 mark)

4. When practising Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.

5. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only a describing word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only an action

6. When practising Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.

   D. Use insults to “practise” Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.

7. When practising Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Charact, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   D. Copy random text without understanding Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Charact.

8. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

9. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. went

10. When practising Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - , which approach is best? (1 mark)

11. When practising Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - , which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .
   B. Use insults to “practise” Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .

12. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. run
   C. quickly
   D. blue

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Fiction and Non- Fiction 4.3.2 Non-Fiction: Autobiography - Structure - Content and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Non-Fiction: Autobiography - Structure - Content and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Literature 5.1.1 Oral Narratives: Trickster Narrative - Features - Function and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Poetry 5.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Language and style: - Alliteration - Assonan and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.

5. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Charact.

8. D — Where is the library?

9. D — went

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .

11. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .

12. B — run

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fiction and Non- Fiction 4.3.2 Non-Fiction: Autobiography - Structure - Content; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Non-Fiction: Autobiography - Structure - Content; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral Literature 5.1.1 Oral Narratives: Trickster Narrative - Features - Function; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Poetry 5.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Language and style: - Alliteration - Assonan; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
